article.title: Why a Customer Can Spend More but Move to a Lower Rank
article.why: Learn the difference between absolute growth and relative rank.

paragraphs.en:
A customer can spend more money this year and still move to a lower rank. This may sound strange, but it happens because a rank is usually relative. It shows where one customer stands compared with other customers.

Imagine that Ken spent 300,000 yen last year and was in the top 10 percent of customers. This year, he spends 330,000 yen. His spending increased by 10 percent, so his own result improved. However, many other customers may have increased their spending by 20 or 30 percent. If the cutoff for the top 10 percent rises to 350,000 yen, Ken will leave the top group even though he spends more than before.

This example shows the difference between absolute value and relative position. Absolute value asks, ‘How much did this customer spend?’ Relative position asks, ‘How does this customer compare with everyone else?’ Both questions are useful, but they describe different things.

The same issue appears when companies use four membership tiers. A customer may increase annual spending from 200,000 to 220,000 yen but move from Tier 2 to Tier 3 if the thresholds are recalculated from the population every year. If managers look only at the tier movement, they may incorrectly think the customer became less valuable.

For a better analysis, track both measures. Show each customer’s spending change and rank change. You can then separate customers into useful patterns: spending up and rank up, spending up but rank down, spending down but rank up, and spending down and rank down.

The second pattern is especially interesting. It means the customer is growing, but not as quickly as the surrounding population. The business may still want to understand and support that customer rather than treating the lower rank as simple deterioration.

Ranks are useful for comparing customers at one point in time. Absolute values are useful for measuring individual change. When analyzing customer growth, use both so that a relative decline does not hide real progress.
paragraphs.zh:
顧客今年消費增加，rank仍可能下降，因為rank通常是相對位置。假設Ken去年消費30萬日圓並位於top 10%，今年增加到33萬，但其他顧客成長更快，使top 10%門檻升到35萬，他就會掉出top group。這不代表他的absolute value惡化，而是relative position下降。

分析時應同時追蹤spending change與rank change，區分「金額升、rank升」「金額升、rank降」等情況。特別是金額上升但rank下降，代表顧客仍在成長，只是成長速度低於周圍population。
paragraphs.ja:
今年の利用額が増えてもrankが下がることがあります。rankは通常、他の顧客と比べた相対的位置だからです。昨年30万円でtop 10%だった顧客が今年33万円へ増えても、他の顧客がさらに大きく伸び、top 10%のthresholdが35万円になればrankは下がります。absolute valueは改善していてもrelative positionは低下します。

分析ではspending changeとrank changeを同時に追跡し、「金額増・rank増」「金額増・rank減」などに分けると有効です。金額が増えてrankが下がった顧客は悪化したのではなく、周囲より成長速度が遅かった可能性があります。

vocabulary.usage: A lower rank is not always deterioration.

business.term: The customer’s absolute spend increased even though the relative rank declined.
business.explanation: 用於區分顧客自身成長與相對排名變化。

sources: Relative ranking and longitudinal customer-value analysis.
